newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly down at 8.2952 against the U.S. dollar on Sunday from Wednesday's 8.2948 on selling in late trading, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2945.
The market was closed from Thursday to Saturday for the Labour Day holiday.

The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2948 and moved in a narrow range around 8.2950 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2945 and a low of 8.2955. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2950, traders said.
The yuan moved steadily around the key 8.2950 level for most of the session despite its slight dip at the close, indicating pro-yuan sentiment was still strong, traders said.

One dealer said the yuan moved little on Sunday with both buyers and sellers having no intention to push the rate sharply up or down right after the three-day break. But abrupt selling in the last few minutes of trading made it end slightly lower.
"Market sentiment has not changed much despite today's fall," said a second dealer. "The yuan is likely to continue to move around the 8.2950 level on Monday."
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 6.5400 from 6.5290 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly lower at 1.0715 from 1.0713 against the Hong Kong dollar.
